how_to_use: Animal story featuring fawn, elephant, monkey, bear. Can also use to talk about kindness, friendship and family.
Give children ‘half’ of each opposite pair and ask children to find the other in the story. Why do they think that the king has become thin?
Introduce the concept of verbs. Pick out and discuss specific verbs in the story: racing; leapt; ran; stumbled etc.
Points to think about:Without much description from the text, how did you make the picture of the king and the dog more detailed in your mind?
For early readers to read alone. To guess what might happen. E.g. ask what might happen after the king runs for many days. Also to talk about opposites.

Without much description from the text, how did the children make the picture of the king and the dog more detailed in their mind?

This story can be used for early readers to read alone. For a prediction exercise, ask the children what might happen after the king runs for many days. This is also a good story to talk about opposites.
This is an animal story featuring a fawn, elephant, monkey and a bear. This story can be used to talk about kindness, friendship and family.
This story can be used to introduce verbs. Pick out and discuss specific verbs in the story, like racing, leapt, ran, stumbled.
